skills.summary: Map assets, trust boundaries and likely attacks
skills.job: Build a lightweight threat model of a feature or system and list ranked mitigations
triggers: threat model this feature
what could go wrong security wise with this design
where are the trust boundaries in my app
gotchas: A threat list with fifty equal items is ignored
Models drawn from the diagram on a slide miss the admin tools, cron jobs and debug endpoints that exist in the code
Authorisation is the most common gap

skills.summary: Triage audit findings by real exposure
skills.job: Triage dependency vulnerability reports by whether the code reaches the flaw, then plan upgrades
triggers: npm audit shows lots of vulnerabilities
which of these CVEs actually matter
help me fix dependabot alerts
gotchas: Running `npm audit fix --force` can install major versions with breaking changes
A critical score on a dev only build tool is often lower real risk than a medium one in a request handler
Lockfile edits by hand drift from the manifest

skills.summary: Find leaked keys and credentials in a repo
skills.job: Find hardcoded secrets in code, config and git history, and set up prevention
triggers: scan my repo for leaked secrets
did I commit an api key
set up a pre-commit check for secrets
gotchas: Rewriting git history without rotating the key leaves the secret valid
High entropy strings include hashes, ids and build outputs
Secrets also hide in Docker images, CI logs, issue comments, notebooks and compiled front-end bundles

skills.summary: Review login, session and token handling
skills.job: Review authentication, session and token handling for weaknesses in an existing implementation
triggers: review my login code
is my jwt handling safe
check how sessions work in this app
gotchas: JWTs cannot be revoked by default
Accepting `alg
Login that says which of user or password was wrong, or reset that says the email is unknown, enables account enumeratio

skills.summary: Check every entry point validates input
skills.job: Audit entry points for missing validation, unsafe parsing and output encoding gaps
triggers: audit input validation in this api
are we validating user input properly
find places that trust user data
gotchas: Blocklists of bad characters are bypassed by encoding tricks
Validating before decoding, or decoding twice, lets encoded payloads slip past the check
JSON parsers accept duplicate keys and large numbers differently, so two layers can disagree about the value

skills.job: Find SQL and query-language injection risks in code and replace string building with parameters
triggers: check my code for sql injection
is this query safe
how do I fix string concatenated queries
gotchas: Escaping functions are brittle and depend on character sets
Stored values are untrusted too
ORMs are not immune

skills.summary: Find cross-site scripting and tighten CSP
skills.job: Find cross-site scripting sinks in a web app and design a Content Security Policy that holds
triggers: check my app for xss
write a content security policy
is it safe to render this user html
gotchas: A CSP with `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'` for scripts gives little protection
Encoding must match the context
Sanitising on input and trusting it everywhere later breaks when the same data feeds a different context

skills.summary: Review CORS rules for over-permissive origins
skills.job: Review CORS configuration to allow the needed origins and block dangerous combinations
triggers: check my cors settings
cors error in the browser, how do I fix it safely
is allowing all origins ok
gotchas: CORS does not stop requests reaching the server
Reflecting any `Origin` with credentials allowed lets any site read a logged-in user's data
A regex like `example

skills.summary: Check password hashing and reset handling
skills.job: Review how passwords are hashed, stored and checked, and plan a safe migration to a stronger scheme
triggers: how should I store passwords
review our password hashing
migrate from md5 to a better hash
gotchas: Adding a salt to SHA-256 does not make it a password hash
Cost settings copied from an old tutorial are too low for current hardware
A site-wide secret (pepper) helps only if it lives outside the database, for example in a secrets manager

skills.summary: Audit and set HTTP security response headers
skills.job: Audit HTTP response headers and set a safe baseline for a web app or API
triggers: check my security headers
add hsts and other headers
what headers should my site send
gotchas: HSTS with a long age on a domain that still has an HTTP-only subdomain locks users out for months
Headers set by both the app and the proxy appear twice, and browsers may take the stricter or ignore both
Error pages, redirects and static assets often miss headers that the main app adds

skills.summary: Vet packages and build pipeline for tampering
skills.job: Vet third party packages and the build pipeline for takeover, typosquat and tampering risk
triggers: is this npm package safe to add
check my dependencies for malicious packages
harden our build against supply chain attacks
gotchas: Download counts are easy to inflate and prove nothing about safety
A trusted package can be compromised by a maintainer account takeover
The repository on the registry page may differ from the published tarball

skills.summary: Rotate a leaked or aging credential safely
skills.job: Rotate a credential without downtime: find every use, issue the new one, switch, revoke the old one, verify
triggers: i leaked an api key, what now
rotate our database password
set up regular key rotation
gotchas: Revoking first and deploying after causes the outage that rotation should avoid
Forgotten consumers (cron hosts, old staging, a teammate's script) fail silently after revocation
Deleting the key from git is not rotation

skills.summary: Trim cloud and app permissions to what is needed
skills.job: Review IAM roles, policies and application permissions and reduce them to what each identity needs
triggers: review our iam policies
this role has too many permissions
write a minimal policy for this service
gotchas: Removing a permission that a rare job uses (monthly report, disaster recovery) breaks it months later
`PassRole` or the ability to edit policies lets an identity grant itself more
Resource wildcards inside an allowed action, such as all buckets, can be broader than the action list suggests

skills.summary: Make user file uploads safe to accept and serve
skills.job: Review or build an upload feature that validates content, limits size, stores safely and serves without risk
triggers: make file uploads secure
review my upload endpoint
users can upload avatars, what could go wrong
gotchas: The `Content-Type` header and the extension are chosen by the client
SVG is XML that can carry script
Image libraries have had parsing bugs

skills.summary: Log security events without logging secrets
skills.job: Define which security events to log, with what fields, and make sure logs help detect abuse without leaking data
triggers: what security events should we log
add audit logging
we need to detect brute force attempts
gotchas: Logging the failed username field often captures a password typed into it
Logs that anyone with app access can edit are useless as evidence after a compromise
Too much logging buries the signal and costs money

skills.summary: Find and block server-side request forgery
skills.job: Find places where the server fetches user-supplied URLs and add allow lists and network controls
triggers: check for ssrf
my app fetches a url from the user, is that safe
block access to internal addresses from webhooks
gotchas: Checking the hostname string is not enough
Validating the URL and then fetching it lets DNS return a different address on the second lookup
A redirect from an allowed host to an internal one defeats a check done only on the first URL

skills.summary: Walk a web app through the OWASP Top 10
skills.job: Walk a web application or API through the OWASP Top 10 categories with concrete checks for this codebase
triggers: run through the owasp top 10 on my app
security checklist before launch
audit my api against owasp
gotchas: A checklist pass does not mean the app is secure
Category names and order differ between editions
Skimming ten endpoints finds the pattern; skipping the unusual ones (exports, admin, imports) misses the bug
